mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in WORKPLACES mobility reduces commuting-linked spending and incidental shopping, so RETAIL_REC will decline further over the next four weeks even if grocery and park activity stay elevated.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below its prior three-week level.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises above TRANSIT by a wide margin, trips consolidate around essentials and discretionary retail is displaced, causing RETAIL_REC to weaken within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds TRANSIT by more than 5 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to its prior two-week mean after GROCERY_PHARM stays more than 5 points above TRANSIT for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PARKS mobility after a local outdoor-activity peak signals less weekend leisure substitution, which shifts demand back toward indoor retail and raises RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls at least 3 points from its recent weekly high
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days after PARKS drops at least 3 points from its recent weekly high.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT collapses while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, fewer mixed-purpose trips reach commercial districts and retail visits fall within one week, reflecting mobility suppression rather than demand substitution.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 4 points week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL stays above 6 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the next weekly mean after TRANSIT drops more than 4 points while RESIDENTIAL remains above 6 points.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT followed by a rebound in WORKPLACES restores weekday circulation into shopping corridors, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL activity stays elevated for multiple weeks, people substitute home-based routines for discretionary outings, so RETAIL_REC declines within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 6 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decrease relative to its prior two-week average after RESIDENTIAL remains above 6 points for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and fall in WORKPLACES marks a shift toward essential, shorter trips; under that regime, discretionary retail weakens over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while WORKPLACES falls for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days after GROCERY_PHARM rises and WORKPLACES falls for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state leisure season, rising PARKS together with modestly rising TRANSIT signals substitution toward outdoor and nonretail trips, which keeps RETAIL_REC flat or lower over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next weekly mean despite PARKS and TRANSIT both increasing from their recent levels.
